prompt:
You are helping a library find out which of its historical works AI models know. Answer from your own memory only. Never invent a quotation.

Each numbered work below is given by its title, the year of the edition we hold and its language. The author's name is withheld; where the title printed it, it is replaced by […].

For each work give:
- "known": do you know this specific work? "yes", "no" or "unsure".
- "author": who wrote it, in Latin script (romanised if necessary), or "unknown".
- "author_native": the author's name in the work's own script if that is not the Latin script, else "".
- "author_is_guess": true if the author is your best guess rather than something you know, else false.
- "date": roughly when the work was written or first published, or "unknown".
- "about": one line on what the work is about, or "unknown".

Works:
1. Title: Pramāṇavārttika — with Manorathanandin’s Vṛtti (Sanskrit) | Year of this edition: 1968 | Language: Sanskrit
2. Title: Catuḥśataka (Sanskrit fragments + Tibetan, ed. V. Bhattacharya) | Language: Sanskrit
3. Title: a fourteenth century sa-skya-pa commentary on santideva's bodhisattvacaryavatara | Language: Tibetan
4. Title: Commentary on Nāgārjuna's Suhṛllekha (Letter to a Friend) | Year of this edition: 1200 | Language: Tibetan
5. Title: Trattato della pietra filosofale e delle sue virtù | Year of this edition: 1588 | Language: Italian
6. Title: Traité de la lumière cachée des métaux | Year of this edition: 1636 | Language: French
7. Title: Elementa (Elements) | Year of this edition: 1482 | Language: Latin

Return ONLY a JSON array with one object per work, in order: [{"i":1,"known":"...","author":"...","author_native":"...","author_is_guess":false,"date":"...","about":"..."}, ...]
